reference.source: Volpe's Neurology of the Newborn / Nelson Textbook of Paediatrics
clinicalPearls: A malformation characterised by a full-thickness cleft extending from the pial surface to the lateral ventricle, lined throughout by grey matter, usually polymicrogyric cortex
It is classified as closed-lip when the cleft walls are apposed or open-lip when they are separated by cerebrospinal fluid, and it may be unilateral or bilateral
The grey-matter lining distinguishes it from an acquired porencephalic cyst, which is lined by white matter or gliotic tissue
It is frequently associated with absence of the septum pellucidum and with optic nerve hypoplasia, overlapping with septo-optic dysplasia
Most cases are thought to result from a destructive vascular or disruptive insult to the developing cortex, though some carry genetic contributions such as EMX2 variants

Clinical features vary with size and laterality, from hemiparesis and focal epilepsy in unilateral closed-lip clefts to severe global delay, spasticity, and refractory seizures in bilateral open-lip disease
Diagnosis is by MRI demonstrating the grey-matter-lined cleft, with evaluation for associated midline and optic anomalies
reference.pathophysiology: Schizencephaly is a disorder of cortical formation in which a cleft lined by dysplastic grey matter spans the full thickness of the hemisphere from the ventricle to the cortical surface. It is thought to arise most often from a disruptive prenatal insult, such as a vascular event, that damages the germinal zone and developing cortex, sometimes combined with genetic susceptibility affecting cortical patterning. Because the injury occurs while the cortex is still developing, the cleft becomes lined by abnormal, typically polymicrogyric grey matter, and associated failure of midline structures such as the septum pellucidum and optic apparatus is common.
additionalDifferentials: Porencephaly, which is lined by white matter or glial tissue rather than grey matter
Open-lip schizencephaly versus severe hydrocephalus or hydranencephaly
Arachnoid cyst communicating with the ventricle
additionalInvestigations: Brain MRI to confirm the grey-matter-lined transmantle cleft and its laterality and type
Assessment of the septum pellucidum and optic nerves for associated septo-optic dysplasia
Ophthalmological examination for optic nerve hypoplasia
Endocrine evaluation of the hypothalamic-pituitary axis when midline anomalies are present
Genetic evaluation including EMX2 and cortical malformation testing where indicated
redFlags: Endocrine dysfunction when associated with septo-optic dysplasia
Progressive macrocephaly or raised intracranial pressure in large open-lip clefts
Visual impairment from optic nerve hypoplasia
reference.prognosis: Prognosis depends on the size, type, and laterality of the cleft. Unilateral closed-lip schizencephaly may cause only mild hemiparesis and manageable epilepsy, whereas bilateral open-lip disease is typically associated with severe motor and cognitive disability and refractory seizures.
pitfalls: Mistaking schizencephaly for a porencephalic cyst by failing to identify the grey-matter lining
Overlooking associated absence of the septum pellucidum and optic nerve hypoplasia
Not screening for hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction when septo-optic features coexist
Confusing a large open-lip cleft with hydrocephalus or hydranencephaly on imaging
management: No specific therapy corrects the malformation, so management targets its neurological consequences
Control focal or refractory epilepsy with antiseizure medication, escalating to epilepsy surgery evaluation in drug-resistant cases
Treat spasticity and hemiparesis with physiotherapy, occupational therapy, orthotics and antispasticity measures such as botulinum toxin or baclofen
Provide developmental, educational and speech and language support for cognitive delay
Screen for and manage associated septo-optic dysplasia, replacing deficient hypothalamic-pituitary hormones and treating visual impairment from optic nerve hypoplasia
Coordinate multidisciplinary paediatric neurology, neurosurgery, ophthalmology, endocrinology and rehabilitation care
Offer genetic evaluation and counselling where a genetic cause such as an EMX2 variant is identified
